claims.text: Corrosion-related degradation or retention of protection in Q235 steel is governed by formation of a protective oxide layer.
Temperature and salt-exposure conditions influence formation of the protective oxide layer.
The protective oxide layer acts as a barrier to corrosion.
At higher temperatures, the oxide layer forms more rapidly.
At higher temperatures, oxide-layer stability and adhesion may be compromised.
Compromised oxide-layer stability and adhesion decrease corrosion protection.
Q235 steel at 700 °C will exhibit a 20% increase in corrosion resistance compared with salt-exposed Q235 steel at room temperature.
Q235 steel at 900 °C will exhibit a 30% decrease in corrosion resistance compared with Q235 steel at 700 °C.
The proposed mechanism applies from room temperature to 900 °C at salt concentrations from 0% to 10%.
Outside the stated temperature and salt-concentration ranges, corrosion mechanisms may differ.
Other corrosive species may influence corrosion-related degradation or retention of protection in Q235 steel.
The microstructure of Q235 steel may influence its corrosion-related degradation or retention of protection.
Failure of the 900 °C corrosion rate to exceed the 700 °C corrosion rate by more than 10% would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The prediction is expressed as a 30% decrease in corrosion resistance at 900 °C, whereas the falsification rule uses a greater-than-10% increase in corrosion rate. No relationship between resistance and rate is defined, so the rule does not directly test the stated quantitative prediction.
